steps.title: Hold one share of the parent
steps.body: A single share of the listed parent is usually enough. The RHP sets the exact rule, so check it for each IPO.

steps.title: Have it in demat by the RHP date
steps.body: Eligibility is fixed on the date of the red herring prospectus, often about a week before the IPO opens. Buy at least a day before so the trade settles.

steps.title: Apply in the shareholder category
steps.body: Bid up to ₹2 lakh as a shareholder. You can still apply as retail or HNI too, and the two are not counted as multiple bids.

steps.title: A separate pool to be allotted from
steps.body: The quota, up to 10% of the issue, is allotted only among eligible shareholders. That pool is apart from retail, not instead of it.

sections.empty: No upcoming IPO has a shareholder quota right now. We check every day.

buy.title: Buy before
buy.hint: Dates are set, or the last day to buy the parent is known. Buy one parent share before that day to bid in the quota.

approved.title: SEBI approved
approved.hint: SEBI has cleared the draft. Dates usually follow within months, so these are next in line.

filed.title: DRHP filed
filed.hint: The draft offer document has a shareholder quota and waits for SEBI. This can take months, and the quota can still change.

rumoured.title: Rumoured
rumoured.hint: A listed company's board has approved taking a group company public, but no draft is filed yet. Plans like these can change or take years.

closed.title: Bidding closed
closed.hint: Bidding has shut for these. Buying the parent now will not get you the quota.

listed.title: Recently listed
listed.hint: Quota IPOs that listed in the last six months. The quota is over for these.

items.q: What is a shareholder quota in an IPO?
items.a: When a listed company takes a subsidiary or group company public, the IPO can set aside up to 10% of the issue for the listed parent's shareholders. Only people who hold the parent's shares on the eligibility date can bid in that portion.

items.q: When do I need to own the parent's shares?
items.a: On the date of the red herring prospectus (RHP), or the record date the RHP names. The shares must be in your demat account by then, so a purchase on that day may be too late.

items.q: Can the shareholder quota be dropped?
items.a: Yes. A draft offer document (DRHP) can change before the final RHP, and a company that only announced an IPO has not committed to anything yet. That is why each IPO here shows its stage and a link to its offer document.

We check offer documents filed with SEBI, NSE and BSE every day for a shareholder reservation and the parent it names. We also read BSE announcements from listed companies whose board has approved taking a subsidiary public; our team reviews each one before it shows here as rumoured. Once an IPO lists it moves to Recently listed for six months. It drops off sooner when a SEBI approval lapses without dates, or when a rumour has no draft after a year.

disclaimer: This list is gathered from offer documents, exchange filings and exchange announcements. Our team reviews every board-stage rumour before it appears; the rest is gathered automatically and not checked by hand. It is not a recommendation to buy any share, and IPO Milega accepts no responsibility for losses arising from any investment decision. A shareholder quota is only final once it appears in the RHP. card.closedNote: Bidding has closed, so the quota is no longer open.
card.buyByNote: Buy the parent before 3:30 PM IST on the last day. Shares settle the next trading day, so a later trade misses the record date.

stageNote.dates: The RHP is out, so the eligibility date may already have passed. Check the RHP before you buy the parent.
stageNote.approved: SEBI has cleared the draft. Dates usually follow within months. Hold the parent before the RHP date.
stageNote.filed: The draft offer document has a shareholder quota. It is waiting for SEBI's approval.
stageNote.announced: The quota comes from the company's announcement. There is no offer document yet, so it could still change.

card.buyingClosedNote: The market closed at 3:30 PM IST on the last day, so buying the parent no longer qualifies. Only earlier holders can bid in the quota.
